name: Stepper motor driver
description: Dual H-bridge current-chopping driver with microstepping (integrated driver IC) and step/dir or SPI control.
electrical_characteristics: Current regulation by chopping; sense resistors set the current
Supply well above the motor's rated voltage for torque at speed
critical_electrical_constraints: Motor current declared; phase traces sized
Sense resistors per the driver datasheet with Kelvin layout
Thermal pad vias; driver thermal limit at the set current
stackup_recommendations: 2 layers 2 oz for drives up to a few amps; 4 layers with inner ground and power for higher current or sensitive current sensing
placement_rules: Half-bridge pairs: high-side and low-side MOSFETs and the DC-link capacitor as tight as possible
Gate driver adjacent to its MOSFETs; bootstrap capacitor at the driver
Current-sense resistor in the phase or DC-link path with a Kelvin pair to the amplifier
Motor connector at the edge nearest the bridge; logic and encoder inputs on the opposite side
routing_rules: Phase and DC-link copper as polygons sized for the peak current and the switching ripple
Gate traces short, with the return on the adjacent layer; gate resistor at the driver
Current-sense traces as a tightly coupled pair to the amplifier; no vias on the Kelvin pair
Encoder/hall signals away from phase copper; filtered at the entry
copper_ground_requirements: Power ground polygon separate from signal ground, joined at the sense resistor or at the controller
thermal_considerations: Conduction loss I^2*Rds(on) at max junction temperature plus switching loss; junction temperature with margin at the motor stall current where stall is possible
emi_emc_considerations: Switching edges controlled by gate resistors; snubbers across the bridge when ringing is measured
Shielded motor cable and common-mode choke footprint for long cables
protection_requirements: Over-current trip from the sense amplifier to the driver's fault input
DC-link over-voltage clamp or brake chopper for regenerative loads
Reverse polarity and inrush limiting on the DC input
verification_requirements: Peak and continuous phase currents declared; bridge devices rated with margin
Trace widths and polygon widths from IPC-2221 for the peak current
Dead-time and gate-drive values recorded from the driver datasheet
Connectivity of every phase and sense net; DRC with clearance for the DC-link voltage
manufacturing_constraints: 2 oz copper; large solder pads on power devices; thermal reliefs off on power pads
unsupported_conditions: Motor disconnected while powered (driver damage): note in the design record
